topic: What happens if lightning strikes you?
title: Struck By Lightning
hook: What if lightning hit you right now?

beats.line: A lightning bolt is about five times hotter than the surface of the sun.
But the current often flashes over your skin instead of through you.
That's why about nine in ten people who get struck survive.
Your heart can stop for a moment, so fast CPR saves lives.
Some survivors get red, fern-shaped marks on their skin that fade in days.

end.line: Would you still stand outside in a storm?

description: Hotter than the sun, yet most people survive it: what a lightning strike really does.

facts.claim: A lightning bolt can heat the air to about 50,000 F, about five times hotter than the surface of the sun.
facts.source: NOAA / National Weather Service - Lightning science

facts.claim: Current can flash over the outside of the body (flashover).
About 90% of people struck by lightning survive.
facts.source: National Weather Service / CDC - Lightning safety

facts.claim: Cardiac arrest is the main cause of lightning death; CPR can save victims.
facts.source: National Weather Service - Medical aspects of lightning

facts.claim: Lichtenberg figures are fern-like skin marks that usually fade within hours to days.
